study type: retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort
exposure: Preeclampsia status (normotensive, new-onset preeclampsia, chronic hypertension with superimposed preeclampsia)
outcome: Heart rate variability (low-frequency, high-frequency, low-/high-frequency ratio, time-domain HRV)
cohort: 70 postpartum women, including normotensive controls, those with new-onset preeclampsia, and those with superimposed preeclampsia.
finding: Postpartum women with preeclampsia, both with and without chronic hypertension, exhibited lower heart rate variability compared to normotensive controls, while higher blood pressure variability was specific to those with non-superimposed preeclampsia.
